candidates.teaser: A parasite living inside a third of all humans right now may be quietly rewriting their personalities — and scientists can prove it.
candidates.video_title: The Parasite Living in Your Brain Right Now
candidates.video_description: Toxoplasma gondii infects roughly 2 billion people worldwide and has been linked to personality shifts, risk-taking behavior, and even schizophrenia. It was first discovered manipulating mice — making them attracted to cats so the parasite could complete its life cycle.
candidates.script: A parasite is living inside roughly 2 billion people right now — and it's changing who they are. Toxoplasma gondii rewires infected mice to run toward cats instead of away, so it can complete its life cycle. In humans, studies link it to higher risk-taking, slower reaction times, and elevated schizophrenia rates. It has no cure. It never fully leaves. And standard blood tests won't even flag it. Are you one of the 2 billion?

candidates.topic: The Dybbuk Box — Most Haunted Object Sold on eBay
candidates.teaser: Someone listed a wine cabinet on eBay with a warning: every owner suffered the same nightmare, the same illness, the same word whispered in their sleep.
candidates.video_title: The Cursed Box That Broke Every Owner
candidates.video_description: The Dybbuk Box is a wine cabinet sold on eBay in 2003 with a haunting disclaimer — every person who owned it reported identical nightmares, hair loss, and the smell of cat urine and jasmine. It now sits locked in a museum no one is allowed to open.
candidates.script: Every single owner of this wine cabinet reported the exact same nightmare — a hag with no eyes, the smell of jasmine and cat urine, waking up with welts. Sold on eBay in 2003 by a Holocaust survivor's grandson, the Dybbuk Box passed through six owners in one year. Each one returned it. One had a stroke. One lost all their hair. It now sits sealed inside a museum, and the curator refuses to open it. What would you do with it?

candidates.topic: The Exploding Lake — Lake Nyos CO2 Catastrophe
candidates.teaser: One night in 1986, a lake in Africa quietly exhaled — and by morning, 1,700 people within miles were dead without a single mark on their bodies.
candidates.video_title: The Lake That Silently Killed 1,700 People
candidates.video_description: Lake Nyos in Cameroon erupted in 1986 — not with lava, but with a sudden release of 1.6 million tonnes of CO2. The invisible cloud suffocated everything in its path within minutes, leaving bodies with no visible injuries. The lake is still loaded with gas today.
candidates.script: In 1986, a lake in Cameroon killed 1,700 people overnight — and left no marks on a single body. Lake Nyos had been silently storing 1.6 million tonnes of CO2 on its floor for decades. One night, the pressure broke. A wall of invisible gas rolled through villages at 100 kilometers per hour, suffocating every living thing within 25 kilometers in minutes. Livestock, birds, insects — all dead. The lake is still full of gas right now. How close would you have to live before you'd move away?

candidates.topic: The Clockwork Soldier — Antoine Louis & the Guillotine Paradox
candidates.teaser: The man who invented a machine to make execution more humane ended up being executed by his own invention — but that's not even the strangest part of the story.
candidates.video_title: He Invented the Guillotine. It Killed Him.
candidates.video_description: Dr. Joseph-Ignace Guillotin proposed a painless execution device as a humanitarian reform during the French Revolution. He never built it — Antoine Louis did. And the question that haunted physicians for years after: do severed heads remain conscious, and for how long?
candidates.script: He proposed the guillotine as an act of mercy — equal, instant, painless for all. Dr. Guillotin never built it; a surgeon named Antoine Louis did, in 1792. Within two years, it had killed over 2,700 people in Paris alone. But the detail that haunted physicians: after decapitation, some heads reportedly blinked and moved their eyes for up to 13 seconds. Scientists still debate whether consciousness survives the blade — even briefly. The man who wanted to end suffering may have created a new kind of it.

candidates.topic: The Island That Appears and Disappears — Sandy Island
candidates.teaser: For over a century, every world map showed an island the size of Manhattan — until a research ship sailed to its exact coordinates and found nothing but open ocean.
candidates.video_title: The Island on Every Map That Doesn't Exist
candidates.video_description: Sandy Island appeared on maps between Australia and New Caledonia for over 100 years, included in Google Earth, the Times Atlas, and official naval charts. In 2012, Australian scientists sailed directly to its coordinates and found only 1,400 meters of open ocean beneath them.
candidates.script: For 137 years, every official world map showed an island the size of Manhattan sitting between Australia and New Caledonia. It had a name — Sandy Island. It was on Google Earth. It was in the Times World Atlas. In 2012, a research vessel sailed directly to its marked coordinates. The ocean was 1,400 meters deep there. No island. Not even a reef. Just open water. No one knows how a phantom landmass fooled the entire world for over a century. What else is wrong on the map?
